rows.heading: What this means for transfusion diagnostics suppliers

items.text: Mandatory donor screening and pretransfusion testing tie revenue to collection and transfusion volumes, not budgets.
Software & services grow fastest (9.17%); leaders bundle analyzers, connectivity, QC and assured reagent supply.
Donor-screening markers, plasma qualification and Asia Pacific outgrow the market and reward early positioning.
The top six hold 57.9%, and country leadership splits between QuidelOrtho and Bio-Rad, leaving fragmented markets open.

slides.title: Demand Drivers & Constraints
slides.subtitle: Why demand is regulated, recurring and increasingly automated

slides.title: Mandatory screening keeps demand regulation-driven; infrastructure gaps and fragmented rules shape who captures it
slides.source: Grand View Research, Blood Bank Serology Market Analysis and Segment Forecast to 2033 (2026)

items.title: Infectious disease marker screening
items.text: WHO recommends screening every donation for HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and syphilis, creating recurring demand for assays, calibrators and controls.

items.title: Red cell typing & compatibility testing
items.text: ABO/RhD typing, antibody screening, identification and crossmatching precede every issue of compatible blood.

items.title: Automation of serology workflows
items.text: Higher sample volumes and traceability needs push labs toward automated grouping, antibody and DAT platforms.

items.title: Uneven infrastructure & QA capacity
items.text: Resource-limited blood services stay manual or semi-automated; advanced systems concentrate in reference labs.

items.title: Regulatory fragmentation
items.text: Assay classification, validation and marker panels differ by country, multiplying technical files and registrations.

items.title: Reagent handling & supply continuity
items.text: Shelf life, cold chain, batch acceptance testing and stock rotation shape purchasing beyond price.

items.title: Plasma fractionation testing
items.text: Growing plasma collection requires qualified-donation screening (HBsAg, anti-HIV, anti-HCV) before fractionation.

items.title: Specialized reagents for complex compatibility
items.text: Anti-CD38 therapy interference creates need for DTT-treated cells, soluble CD38 and related reagents.

items.title: Asia Pacific capacity build-out
items.text: Asia Pacific is the fastest-growing region at 8.08% CAGR, reaching USD 1,761.6 Mn by 2033.

rows.label: Implication
rows.text: Suppliers that combine regulatory depth, automation and assured reagent supply are best placed to convert mandated demand into share.

slides.title: Implications
slides.subtitle: Where to play to capture the USD 2.6 Bn increment

slides.title: Where to play: four moves align suppliers with the segments and regions that create most new revenue
slides.source: Grand View Research, Blood Bank Serology Market Analysis and Segment Forecast to 2033 (2026); increments and share shifts are GVR analysis

items.title: Lead with integrated workflows
items.text:
**Why:** software & services are the fastest product segment and add USD 373.8 Mn.

**How:** bundle analyzers, middleware, QC materials and service into one contract.

items.title: Win donor screening
items.text:
**Why:** TTI serology grows at 7.99%; anti-HBc and HIV Combo alone add USD 392.7 Mn.

**How:** lead with high-throughput CLIA / ECLIA menus for blood centers.

items.title: Build plasma qualification
items.text:
**Why:** plasma fractionation labs are the fastest end user (8.09%), adding USD 497.1 Mn.

**How:** qualified-donation panels (HBsAg, anti-HIV, anti-HCV) for fractionators.

items.title: Prioritise Asia Pacific
items.text:
**Why:** USD 811.6 Mn of new revenue at 8.08% CAGR, the fastest region.

**How:** early access in fragmented markets such as China, where others hold 68.0%.

rows.label: Bottom line
rows.text: Growth is mandated and visible; share goes to suppliers who own the workflow and get there first.
